knowledge:
- key_parameters: expr.matrix=normalized signal intensity matrix with genes in rows and samples in columns ;; cond.a, cond.b, cond.c, cond.d=vectors of column names in expr.matrix representing control and treatment samples for the first and second expression levels ;; label.level=character vector specifying names for the two levels (default "1st level", "2nd level") ;; label.condition=character vector specifying names for the two conditions (default "control", "treated") ;; data.type=type of data, "array" (default) or "ngs" ;; method=statistical method for DEG detection ("limma", "t-test", "RP", "TE", "ANOTA", "DESeq", "edgeR", "none") ;; significance.threshold=threshold on statistical significance (default 0.05) ;; FC.threshold=threshold on absolute log2 fold change (default 0) ;; log.transformed=boolean specifying if data is log2 transformed (default FALSE) ;; mult.cor=boolean specifying if significance threshold is applied to multiple-test corrected p-values (default TRUE) ;; ontology=GO ontology of interest ("CC", "BP", "MF", or "all") ;; classOfDEGs=class of genes for enrichment ("up", "down", "both") ;; test.method=statistical method for GO enrichment ("classic", "elim", "weight", "weight01", "parentchild") ;; test.threshold=significance threshold for GO terms (default 0.05)
- alternatives: For DEG detection, computeDEGs() supports limma, t-test, RP (Rank Products), TE (Translational Efficiency), ANOTA, DESeq, and edgeR. For GO enrichment, GOEnrichment() supports classic, elim, weight, weight01, and parentchild methods from the topGO package.
- when_to_use: Use when comparing high-throughput expression data from two parallel levels (e.g., transcriptome and translatome, or transcriptome and proteome) across two experimental conditions (e.g., treated vs untreated, mutant vs wild-type) to identify translational control and discordant regulation.
- pitfalls: The package does not perform data normalization (except internally for edgeR and DESeq); input signals must be pre-normalized (e.g., quantile normalized for microarrays). Ensure log.transformed is set correctly depending on whether the input data has already been log2-transformed.

workflows.name: translatome_analysis_workflow
workflows.intent: Identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) at two expression levels (transcriptome and translatome), perform GO enrichment on the DEGs, and compare the enriched biological themes between the two levels.
input: expressionMatrix (normalized signal intensity matrix with genes in rows and samples in columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Initialize the TranslatomeDataset object using newTranslatomeDataset() ;; 2. Identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs) at both expression levels using computeDEGs() ;; 3. Perform Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment analysis on the identified DEGs using GOEnrichment() ;; 4. Compare the enriched biological themes between the two expression levels using GOComparison()
workflows.code:
library(tRanslatome) 
data(tRanslatomeSampleData) 
translatome.analysis <- newTranslatomeDataset(expressionMatrix, 
			c("tot.undiff.a", "tot.undiff.b", "tot.undiff.c"), 
			c("tot.diff.a", "tot.diff.b", "tot.diff.c"), 
			c("pol.undiff.a", "pol.undiff.b", "pol.undiff.c"), 
			c("pol.diff.a", "pol.diff.b", "pol.diff.c"), 
			label.level= c("transcriptome", "translatome"), 
			label.condition=c("undifferentiated", "differentiated"))
limma.DEGs <- computeDEGs(translatome.analysis, 
													 method= "limma", mult.cor=TRUE) 
CCEnrichment <- GOEnrichment(limma.DEGs,ontology="CC", classOfDEGs="up",
															test.method="elim", test.threshold = 0.05)
CCComparison <- GOComparison(CCEnrichment)
